articles.title: Ladakh Launches India's First High-Altitude Snow Leopard Safari - GKToday
articles.content: Home Ladakh Launches India’s First High-Altitude Snow Leopard Safari Ladakh Launches India’s First High-Altitude Snow Leopard Safari October 8, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Ladakh launched India’s first high-altitude snow leopard wildlife safari on 7 October 2026, during Wildlife Week celebrations in Leh. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena flagged off six specially designed open-back vehicles. The initiative is a collaboration between the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society and the Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment, UT Ladakh. Ladakh hosts 477 of India’s estimated 718 snow leopards. Snow Leopard Habitat and Distribution The snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a large cat adapted to cold, rugged mountain habitats. Its range extends across the high mountains of Central and South Asia. In India, snow leopards occur in the trans-Himalayan regions of Ladakh and in parts of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh. Rocky slopes and steep terrain provide habitat and cover for the species. The initial safari routes are planned for Rumbak, Shang and Uley, areas known for frequent snow leopard sightings. Planned future routes include Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, as well as Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass. Protected Areas and Conservation Hemis National Park is a high-altitude protected area in Ladakh and forms part of the snow leopard’s habitat. Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary are also among the protected areas associated with the region’s high-altitude ecosystems. Wildlife conservation in these landscapes includes protecting habitats and managing human–wildlife interactions. The safari decision was announced by the Ladakh administration on 5 August 2026 and implemented within two months. The initiative’s stated aims include responsible wildlife tourism, community-based conservation and sustainable livelihoods for local youth and communities. Community-Based Wildlife Tourism Wildlife tourism in snow leopard habitat can involve local communities in visitor services and conservation activities. The Ladakh initiative uses specially designed open-back vehicles and plans to operate in areas with snow leopard sightings. Wildlife Week is observed in India from 2 to 8 October. Important Facts for Exams The scientific name of the snow leopard is Panthera uncia. Hemis National Park is located in Ladakh. Wildlife Week in India is observed from 2 to 8 October. The six safari vehicles were flagged off in Leh on 7 October 2026. Ladakh’s estimated snow leopard population is 477, compared with an estimated 718 across India. Initial safari areas include Rumbak, Shang and Uley. articles.title: Lucknow to Emerge as India's AI Innovation Hub: CM Yogi Adityanath - SMEStreet
articles.content: Sectors Policies Lucknow to Emerge as India’s AI Innovation Hub: CM Yogi Adityanath Uttar Pradesh Govt. plans to establish 50 AI startups in Lucknow and build a strong AI ecosystem, while HCL Tech launches Phase 2 of its IT City with a ₹500 crore investment. SMEStreet Edit Desk 08 Oct 2026 15:06 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the Uttar Pradesh Government is committed to establishing Lucknow among India’s leading AI innovation cities and will develop a strong innovation ecosystem over the next five years. Addressing a programme organised to mark the 10th anniversary of the HCL Tech Lucknow campus, the Chief Minister said the government will extend full support to establish at least 50 world-class AI startups in Lucknow, strengthen them and help them reach global markets. He also urged HCL Tech to partner with the state government in this initiative. The Chief Minister said Lucknow must evolve beyond being an IT services centre and emerge as a major hub for AI, semiconductors, cyber security, computing technology and deep tech, with the government and industry working together to build the ecosystem. He highlighted the transformation in Uttar Pradesh’s technology and infrastructure landscape, noting that the state’s IT and ITES exports have grown from around ₹12,000–15,000 crore a decade ago to over ₹1 lakh crore, with a target of ₹2.5 lakh crore in the next four years. Electronics exports have also increased from around ₹3,800 crore to ₹45,000 crore, with a target of ₹2 lakh crore by 2030. The Chief Minister also noted that IT parks are now operational in Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Meerut and Agra, while new IT parks are being developed in Varanasi, Bareilly, Kanpur and Gorakhpur. Under the new Startup Policy, Noida and Lucknow are being developed as deep-tech hubs, while work is progressing towards developing India’s first AI City and a comprehensive AI ecosystem in Lucknow. On the occasion, the Chief Minister launched Phase-2 of HCL IT City Lucknow. The expansion will develop approximately 9.5 lakh square feet on 20 acres, with an investment of around ₹500 crore. The project will include a new IT building, capacity for around 5,000 seats, multilevel parking and modern facilities, and is expected to create approximately 6,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities. HCL Tech Chairperson Roshni Nadar Malhotra said Uttar Pradesh is the karmabhoomi and home of the HCL Group, adding that the decision to invest in HCL IT City Lucknow reflected the company’s belief that global technology and talent can develop beyond metropolitan cities when the right opportunities and infrastructure are available. She also announced an AI training programme for 1,000 students from local colleges to provide future-ready skills and career opportunities. The Chief Minister also highlighted HCL’s contribution to social development through its programmes in Uttar Pradesh. Over the past 10–11 years, HCL’s programmes have reached more than 50 lakh people and over 3,000 villages, with initiatives focused on rural livelihoods, education and development....

articles.title: Who Is Nigar Shaji? The Project Director of India's Aditya-L1 Solar Mission - Herzindagi
articles.content: Who Is Nigar Shaji? The Project Director of India’s Aditya-L1 Solar Mission Welcome to Herstory, where you will learn about the supertalented women who have created history. Learn about Nigar Shaji, the ISRO scientist and Project Director behind India's maiden solar mission, Aditya-L1. Discover her journey, career, and achievements. Nitisha Sharma Updated:- 2026-10-08, 13:50 IST Herstory is the place where we acknowledge all those women who have accomplished many things and broken many barriers to make a positive difference in the world. Nigar Shaji is an Indian engineer in aerospace who holds the position of a senior space scientist at the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). She became famous in the international arena as the Project Director for the Aditya-L1 project, which was India’s first-ever space-based mission meant to conduct research on the Sun. Having worked at ISRO for more than three decades now, Nigar Shaji has played a crucial role in contributing to the scientific advancements in satellite communication, remote sensing, and interplanetary studies in India. Who Is Nigar Shaji? Nigar Shaji was born in a family of farmers in Sengottai, Tenkasi district of Tamil Nadu. She did her undergraduate studies in Electronics and Communication Engineering in Tirunelveli. She later went on to do her postgraduate studies in Electronics from Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra. In 1987, she joined ISRO’s U R Rao Satellite Centre and has been rising through the ranks as a test engineer for satellites since then. ALSO READ- Who Is Dr Vasudevan? Meet The Woman Reimagining India’s Skilling Ecosystem Nigar Shaji Role As Project Director Of Aditya-L1 Nigar Shaji was the Project Director who managed the execution of the complicated scientific and engineering process involved in the development of Aditya-L1. She successfully led the launch of the satellite in September 2023 and placed it in a halo orbit at the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrangian point to study space weather and phenomena occurring within. Nigar Shaji Contributions To ISRO Before heading up Aditya-L1, Shaji was the Associate Project Director for Resourcesat-2A, an important remote-sensing satellite for India. Her knowledge is not limited to space missions within Earth’s orbit; she has also worked as a study director for the proposed mission to Venus and other planets. Conclusion From Nigar Shaji’s transition from the small town of Tamil Nadu to the directorship of one of ISRO’s most sophisticated missions, it is evident how technically skilled and visionary she is. As the mind behind India’s Aditya-L1 mission, she is an inspiration for many women in STEM. Image credits: Instagram ALSO READ- Who Is Ritu Karidhal? articles.title: AI Aesthetics Launches India's First Dermatologist-Trained AI Treatment Engines for Skin ...
articles.content: VMPL Jaipur (Rajasthan) [India], October 8: AI Aesthetics by Dr. Aakriti Mehra, a dermatologist-led skin clinic in Jaipur's C-Scheme, today announced the full deployment of its proprietary AI treatment engines, a set of clinical decision systems that analyse each client's skin through five-mode facial imaging and design personalised facials, pigmentation plans and IV wellness protocols according to rules written by the clinic's founder. The clinic also confirmed its roadmap: longitudinal skin tracking and AI-set parameters for laser hair removal within one month, and AI-guided hair growth treatments within three months. AI Aesthetics is the first clinic of its kind in Rajasthan, and among the first in India, to run its own dermatologist-trained AI inside the treatment room rather than using generic skin-analysis software. Every engine is built on the clinical constraints, safety rules and treatment philosophy of Dr. Aakriti Mehra, so that the system reasons the way an experienced dermatologist does while the final decision on every treatment remains with the doctor. THREE ENGINES, ONE CLINICAL BRAIN The Facial Engine. A five-mode scan (red, polarised sub-surface, polarised surface, white and Wood's UV light) is converted into a structured feature packet and scored across fifteen parameters, including barrier health, acne, sebum, redness, hydration, luminosity, pigmentation, peri-orbital health, texture and pores, wrinkles, jawline sagging, firmness and radiance. The engine then builds an AI customized facial for that face from the clinic's catalogue of hydradermabrasion probes, chemical peels, carbon laser, radiofrequency, LED and targeted infusions, choosing the hero corrective for each primary concern, treating different facial zones differently, and refusing any step that the doctor's rules exclude for that client on that day, from sun exposure and recent retinol use to pregnancy and facial surface temperature. The IV Engine. The same logic designs IV drip therapy, selecting and dosing glutathione, vitamin C, B12 and other actives against a doctor-led health screen that applies the clinic's exclusions before any cannula is placed. Pigmentation Decode. A dedicated pigmentation module separates tan, post-acne marks, sun spots and melasma-pattern pigment by depth and chronicity, so that pigmentation treatment in Jaipur's high-UV climate is matched to the kind of pigment present rather than applied as a single routine. The engines are already running for every client who books an AI skin analysis or an AI customized facial at the clinic, alongside its established menu of Hydrafacial , carbon facial, chemical peels, HIFU and RF skin tightening, and laser hair removal in Jaipur on a multi-wavelength diode platform. WHAT MAKES THE SYSTEM DIFFERENT * Dermatologist-written rules, not black-box scoring. Every exclusion the engine applies, from "no medium peel within seven days of an event" to "HIFU only between the ages of 30 and 60", is a rule Dr. Mehra wrote, and the clinic publishes those rules on its website. * Zone-level treatment. The engine maps concerns across the forehead, nose, cheeks, chin, perioral and under-eye zones and can prescribe different steps for different zones in the same session. * Built for Indian skin and Jaipur conditions. articles.title: World Space Week 2026: 8 Milestone ISRO Missions That Made India A Space Power
articles.content: News Photogallery science World Space Week 2026: 8 Milestone ISRO Missions That Made India A Space Power World Space Week 2026: 8 Milestone ISRO Missions That Made India A Space Power Published By : Sujata Singh , News18.com Edited By: Priyanka Das Last Updated: October 08, 2026, 11:30 IST From Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, to Chandrayaan-3’s historic lunar landing, these ISRO missions mark some of the biggest milestones in India’s space journey. Share this Article WhatsApp facebook Twitter telegram copy link 1 / 9 From launching its first satellite in the 1970s to reaching the Moon, India’s space programme has come a long way. Over the decades, ISRO’s missions have expanded from basic satellite technology to deep-space exploration and advanced scientific research. As World Space Week is being observed from October 4 to 10, here are eight ISRO missions that mark some of the biggest milestones in India’s space journey. (File Photo) 2 / 9 Aryabhata Launched on April 19, 1975, Aryabhata was India’s first satellite. Built by ISRO and launched with Soviet assistance, it marked the beginning of India’s journey in space-based scientific research. Its experiments focused on areas including X-ray astronomy, solar physics and aeronomy. (Image: ISRO) ADVERTISEMENT 3 / 9 INSAT The INSAT programme transformed the way India used satellites for everyday needs. Its satellites supported telecommunications, television broadcasting, meteorology and education, making space technology directly relevant to life on Earth. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) 4 / 9 PSLV The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) became one of ISRO’s most important launch systems after its first successful mission in 1994. It went on to launch a wide range of Indian and international satellites and played a crucial role in missions including Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) ADVERTISEMENT 5 / 9 Chandrayaan-1 Launched on October 22, 2008, Chandrayaan-1 was India’s first mission to the Moon. The spacecraft carried 11 scientific instruments and mapped the lunar surface. One of its major scientific achievements was providing evidence that significantly advanced the understanding of water on the Moon. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) 6 / 9 Mars Orbiter Mission Also known as Mangalyaan, the Mars Orbiter Mission was launched in 2013. It made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit and demonstrated the country’s ability to undertake interplanetary missions. It also studied the Martian surface and atmosphere. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) ADVERTISEMENT 7 / 9 Chandrayaan-2 Launched on July 22, 2019, Chandrayaan-2 was designed to study the Moon through an orbiter, lander and rover. Although the lander did not achieve a successful soft landing, the orbiter continued its scientific mission and provided valuable lunar data. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) 8 / 9 Chandrayaan-3 On August 23, 2023, Chandrayaan-3 achieved a historic soft landing on the lunar surface. Its lander and rover conducted scientific experiments near the Moon’s south polar region, demonstrating India’s capability to safely land and operate a rover on the lunar surface. articles.title: How InMobi is using AI to transform India's tourism - NewsBytes
articles.content: InMobi signed MoU with Ministry of Tourism How InMobi is using AI to transform India's tourism By Mudit Dube Oct 08, 2026 10:53 am What's the story InMobi, a leading technology company and India's first unicorn, has announced its plan to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to promote tourism in India. The company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Tourism on World Tourism Day, observed annually on September 27. Under the agreement, InMobi and its AI-driven content platform, Glance , will explore digital initiatives designed to promote Indian tourism and widen its global reach. Exploration Linking major tourist destinations to regional circuits InMobi's initiative will link major tourist destinations to regional circuits, nudging visitors toward nearby heritage towns, craft villages, and nature corridors to encourage extended stays. "A trip to an iconic monument can open the door to discovering a nearby heritage enclave, craft village, local food trail, or natural sanctuary," said Dr. Subi Chaturvedi, Global SVP at InMobi. "The core mission is to distribute the dividends of tourism directly to local guides, artisans, homestays, and grassroots businesses." Beyond the list Promoting even spread of tourism InMobi's partnership with the Ministry of Tourism is also aimed at promoting a more even spread of tourism. "We want to inspire visitors to think outside of the 'box' and find out about the amazing places to visit around our nation that are not on their list!" said Chaturvedi. By decongesting high-traffic landmarks, the strategy redistributes tourist footfall to boost local commerce, jobs, and infrastructure in emerging or lesser-known travel destinations. ADVERTISEMENT Heritage tourism 'We want to bring cultural narrative of destinations to life' "Heritage tourism sits at the core of this initiative," said Chaturvedi, who also serves as InMobi's Chief Corporate Affairs and Public Policy Officer. "We want to bring the cultural narrative of these destinations to life: from their historic architecture and spiritual roots to local crafts, food trails, and living traditions." "Our goal is to shine a light not just on famous monuments, but on hidden, local gems that tell equally compelling stories," she added. ADVERTISEMENT Behavioral change Responsible travel behavior also a focus area The MoU also focuses on promoting responsible travel behavior. Content cards will be used to discourage littering, defacement, and vandalism while encouraging respectful etiquette at monuments and heritage sites. The idea is that promoting new destinations goes hand in hand with protecting them. InMobi plans joint thematic campaigns around festivals, national priorities, and international events to attract both domestic and international tourists. Innovative approach Glance to showcase destinations under 'Incredible India' banner Glance, with more than 400 million users worldwide, operates as a smart lock screen platform built into Android smartphones. It delivers real-time news, weather forecasts, games, and AI-curated shopping recommendations without requiring users to unlock their devices. This innovative technology will be used to showcase both popular and offbeat Indian destinations to millions of smartphone users.
